title: test-0001-GEN-DISASTERS
passage: Natural disasters like earthquakes, floods, and cyclones require careful planning. During an earthquake, you must 'Drop, Cover, and Hold on' under a sturdy table. Avoid windows, as glass can shatter and cause injuries. Since scientists cannot predict the exact time or date of an earthquake, families must keep an emergency kit ready at all times. This kit should include 3 liters of water per person per day, non-perishable food, a flashlight, and a battery-operated radio. For floods, never walk or drive through moving water, even if it is only 15 centimeters deep, as it can knock you down. If a flood warning is issued, move to higher ground immediately before water enters your home. After a flood, do not drink clear-looking water without boiling it for at least 1 minute to kill germs. During a cyclone, stay indoors and listen to official weather reports from the India Meteorological Department. Do not trust unverified social media messages. If you are told to evacuate, move to a shelter before the storm arrives. Remember that the 'eye' of the cyclone is a calm area, but it is followed by even stronger winds. Most cyclone-related deaths are actually caused by storm surges, which are giant waves of seawater, rather than just high winds.
summary: Natural disasters like earthquakes, floods, and cyclones require careful planning. For floods, never walk or drive through moving water—no matter how deep it is. If a flood warning is issued, run to higher ground before water enters your home.
